::: section-card
## Data preparation

This section documents the construction of the analytical dataset, including population identifiers, taxonomic matching, phylogenetic filtering, moderator preparation, and random-effect structure checks.
:::

## Packeges

The R packages required for data preparation.




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(ape)
library(brms)
library(maps)
library(knitr)

options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
```
:::




## Import data

### The input files used in the analysis: the mixed-paternity dataset and the dated Clements phylogenetic tree.









This table summarises the main input files used in the analysis, including the size of the raw dataset and the number of tips and internal nodes in the phylogenetic tree.




::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|Item              |Summary                             |
|:-----------------|:-----------------------------------|
|Raw dataset       |676 rows and 39 columns             |
|Phylogenetic tree |11167 tips and 11166 internal nodes |


:::
:::




## Prepare data

### Population identifier

Population identity was defined using study identity and rounded geographic coordinates, with latitude and longitude rounded to two decimal places prior to constructing the population identifier.




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mixed_pat <- mixed_pat_raw %>%
  mutate(
    Lat_round = round(Lat, 2),
    Long_round = round(Long, 2),
    population_id = paste(Study_ID, Lat_round, Long_round, sep = "_"),
    population_id = as.factor(population_id)
  )
```
:::




### Study and species formatting

The following step formats the main grouping variables used in the models and calculates the total number of broods by combining mixed- and non-mixed-brood counts.




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mixed_pat <- mixed_pat %>%
  mutate(
    Study_ID = as.factor(Study_ID),
    species_phylo_brms = as.factor(Clements_name),
    species_nonphylo = as.factor(Clements_name),

    n_mixed_broods = as.numeric(n_mixed_broods),
    n_non_mixed_broods = as.numeric(n_non_mixed_broods),
    n_total_broods = n_mixed_broods + n_non_mixed_broods
  )
```
:::




### Phylogeny preparation

Species names were harmonised between the mixed-paternity dataset and the phylogenetic tree prior to pruning the tree and generating the phylogenetic covariance matrix used in the Bayesian models.




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="true"}
species_data <- mixed_pat %>%
  filter(!is.na(species_phylo_brms)) %>%
  pull(species_phylo_brms) %>%
  as.character() %>%
  unique()

species_tree <- tree$tip.label

species_for_tree <- intersect(species_data, species_tree)

tree_analysis <- ape::keep.tip(tree, species_for_tree)

phylo_mat <- ape::vcv.phylo(tree_analysis, corr = TRUE)

phylo_mat <- phylo_mat[
  sort(rownames(phylo_mat)),
  sort(colnames(phylo_mat))
]

mixed_pat <- mixed_pat %>%
  filter(species_phylo_brms %in% rownames(phylo_mat)) %>%
  mutate(
    species_phylo_brms = droplevels(species_phylo_brms),
    species_nonphylo = droplevels(species_nonphylo)
  )
```
:::




### Phylogeny - summary




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="true"}
phylo_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Species matched to phylogeny",
    "Tips in source tree",
    "Species retained after phylogenetic filtering"
  ),
  Value = c(
    length(species_for_tree),
    length(tree$tip.label),
    n_distinct(mixed_pat$species_phylo_brms)
  )
)

knitr::kable(phylo_summary)
```

### Moderator variable preparation




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
min_n <- 5

mixed_pat <- mixed_pat %>%
  mutate(
    marker_type_model = as.factor(marker_type_model),
    nest_box_model = as.factor(nest_box_model),
    nest_type_model = as.factor(nest_type_model),

    breeding_system = as.factor(breeding_system),
    mono_poly_model = as.factor(mono_poly_model),
    parental_care = as.factor(parental_care),
    cooperative_breeding = as.factor(cooperative_breeding),

    migration = as.factor(migration),
    coloniality = as.factor(coloniality),

    CS_max = as.numeric(CS_max),
    body_mass = as.numeric(body_mass),
    study_duration = as.numeric(study_duration_num),

    Lat_round = round(as.numeric(Lat), 2),
    abs_lat = abs(Lat_round),

    CS_max_sc = as.numeric(scale(CS_max)),
    body_mass_sc = as.numeric(scale(body_mass)),
    study_duration_sc = as.numeric(scale(study_duration)),
    abs_lat_sc = as.numeric(scale(abs_lat))
  )
```
:::




## Preparation of the database

### Database overall study




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
data_overall_study <- mixed_pat %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(n_mixed_broods),
    !is.na(n_non_mixed_broods),
    !is.na(n_total_broods),
    n_total_broods > 0,
    !is.na(Study_ID),
    !is.na(species_phylo_brms)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Study_ID = droplevels(Study_ID),
    species_nonphylo = droplevels(species_nonphylo),
    species_phylo_brms = droplevels(species_phylo_brms),
    population_id = droplevels(population_id)
  )
```
:::




### Database single moderators




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
data_nest_box <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(nest_box_model)) %>%
  droplevels()


data_migration <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(migration)) %>%
  droplevels()

data_coloniality <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(coloniality)) %>%
  droplevels()


data_cooperative <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(cooperative_breeding)) %>%
  droplevels()

data_study_duration <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(study_duration_sc)) %>%
  droplevels()

data_clutch_size <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(CS_max_sc)) %>%
  droplevels()

data_body_mass <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(body_mass), body_mass > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    body_mass = as.numeric(body_mass),
    log_body_mass = log10(body_mass),
    log_body_mass_sc = as.numeric(scale(log_body_mass))
  ) %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(log_body_mass),
    is.finite(log_body_mass_sc)
  ) %>%
  droplevels()

data_abs_latitude <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(abs_lat_sc)) %>%
  droplevels()

data_marker_type <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(marker_type_model)) %>%
  droplevels()


data_nest_type <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(nest_type_model)) %>%
  droplevels()


valid_breeding_levels <- data_overall_study %>%
  count(breeding_system) %>%
  filter(!is.na(breeding_system), n >= 5) %>%
  pull(breeding_system)

data_breeding_system <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(breeding_system),
    breeding_system %in% valid_breeding_levels
  ) %>%
  droplevels()

data_mono_poly <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(mono_poly_model)) %>%
  droplevels()

data_parental_care <- data_overall_study %>%
  filter(!is.na(parental_care)) %>%
  droplevels()
```
:::




## Relationship among candidate random-effects grouping factors

Before fitting the models, we evaluated the degree of overlap and nesting among candidate random-effects grouping factors, including species identity, study identity, and the pragmatic population identifier.




::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|Comparison                | Groups_with_only_one_match| Total_groups| Percent_only_one_match|
|:-------------------------|--------------------------:|------------:|----------------------:|
|Populations per species   |                        275|          375|                   73.3|
|Species per population    |                        581|          597|                   97.3|
|Populations per reference |                        524|          554|                   94.6|
|References per population |                        597|          597|                  100.0|
|References per species    |                        282|          375|                   75.2|
|Species per reference     |                        527|          554|                   95.1|


:::
